recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future changes to ActUSPrivacyLaw code-system or value-set membership should be handled through UTG/THO unless a new Security or Vocabulary work-group decision explicitly changes current FHIR-core security-label guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-23703 was a Published FHIR-core Security work group change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking to remove the security-labels Jurisdiction Specific Security Labels guidance that pointed at deprecated USPrivacyLaw content and to change the referenced value set to ActUSPrivacyLaw.
initial_application: Commit d97f7c47d6 initially applied J#23703 by commenting out the jurisdiction-specific section and changing the US Privacy Law row from v3/ActUSPrivacyLaw/vs.html to terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v3-ActUSPrivacyLaw. Later current-branch history in 28032417e6 removed that commented block entirely while restructuring the security-labels HCS table.
additional_context: The security-labels page is active source under source/hierarchy.xml. The current page no longer contains the old jurisdiction section or local v3/ActUSPrivacyLaw link, while source/terminologies/valueset-security-labels.xml composes http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v3-ActUSPrivacyLaw. FHIR-25171 later raised the same ActUSPrivacyLaw deprecation/UTG concern and was resolved No Change because terminology changes had moved to UTG. Security WG minutes record FHIR-23703 as recommended persuasive and then applied to FHIR core.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was necessary because authoritative current source already avoids the deprecated local guidance and uses the THO ActUSPrivacyLaw canonical where the aggregate security-label value set still needs ActUSPrivacyLaw.
